name: AirtableInsert
title: Airtable Insert
description: Write records to an Airtable table, batched, updating any that carry a record id
whenToUse: Pick to WRITE rows into an Airtable table from upstream data: it batches automatically, updates any record that already carries an Airtable id, and can skip rows whose value is already present. Use it to persist a collection; it writes, it does not read.

package.name: airtable
package.packageFile:
$schema: ../_schema/package.schema.json

# FULLY DECLARATIVE. Three nodes, one base URL, one token.
#
# This package forced TWO executor capabilities, both loops a manifest cannot write itself:
# `paginate` for reading past the first page, and `chunk` for writing a collection when the
# vendor caps a batch at ten. Every list-returning and collection-writing node after this
# one inherits both.
#
# The retired TypeScript is at `_legacy/nodes/airtable/`.

name: airtable
displayName: Airtable
description: Read, check and write Airtable records
version: 2.0.0
category: storage
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1775377626/gravity/icons/airtable.png

features:
  - Fetch records with filters, views and sorting, paginated
  - Check whether a value already exists
  - Insert and update records, batched and deduplicated

allowedHosts:
  - api.airtable.com

requires:
  credential: [bearer]
  transport: [json]
  paginate: [cursor]
  chunk: true
  executorVersion: ">=1.3.0"

credentials.airtableCredential.yaml:
$schema: ../../_schema/credential.schema.json

name: airtableCredential
displayName: Airtable
description: Airtable Personal Access Token for reading and writing to Airtable bases
documentationUrl: https://airtable.com/create/tokens

properties:
  - name: personalAccessToken
    displayName: Personal Access Token
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your Airtable Personal Access Token
    placeholder: pat

shared.rows.yaml:
# The row-splitting expressions, defined ONCE and $ref'd wherever they are needed.
#
# `AirtableInsert` needs "which rows are updates" and "which rows are creates" in three
# places each: the call's `when`, its `chunk.items`, and the skipped count in events. The
# sandbox has no assignment, so there is no way to bind an intermediate value inside an
# expression. A shared fragment is how one definition serves all three, and it is why these
# live here rather than being pasted six times.

# An Airtable record id is "rec" plus 14 characters. A row carrying one is an UPDATE.
isAirtableId: &isAirtableId >-
  return (config.records || []).filter(r =>
    typeof r.id === 'string' && r.id.length === 17 && r.id.slice(0, 3) === 'rec')

# Everything else is a CREATE. `id` is RESERVED by Airtable, so a row carrying its own
# non-Airtable `id` has it renamed to `apollo_id` rather than dropped: the retired code did
# this, and changing it would silently lose a column.
#
# Then anything the dedup field says is already in the table is removed. `calls.existing` is
# the paged read; when dedup is off that call is skipped and there is no key, so the filter
# passes everything through.
toCreate: &toCreate >-
  return (config.records || [])
    .filter(r => !(typeof r.id === 'string' && r.id.length === 17 && r.id.slice(0, 3) === 'rec'))
    .map(r => Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(r).map(e => [e[0] === 'id' ? 'apollo_id' : e[0], e[1]])))
    .filter(r => !String(config.dedupField || '').trim()
      || !((calls.existing || {}).items || [])
           .map(x => String(((x.fields || {})[config.dedupField === 'id' ? 'apollo_id' : config.dedupField]) ?? ''))
           .filter(Boolean)
           .includes(String(r[config.dedupField === 'id' ? 'apollo_id' : config.dedupField] ?? '')))

# Offered minus kept: how many the dedup field dropped.
skipped: &skipped >-
  return (config.records || [])
    .filter(r => !(typeof r.id === 'string' && r.id.length === 17 && r.id.slice(0, 3) === 'rec'))
    .length
  - (calls.creates ? calls.creates.sent : 0)

# The same set, as a boolean, for the call's `when`. Defined next to it so the two cannot
# drift: a `when` that disagreed with `items` would either skip a needed write or send an
# empty one.
toCreateAny: &toCreateAny >-
  return (config.records || [])
    .filter(r => !(typeof r.id === 'string' && r.id.length === 17 && r.id.slice(0, 3) === 'rec'))
    .filter(r => !String(config.dedupField || '').trim()
      || !((calls.existing || {}).items || [])
           .map(x => String(((x.fields || {})[config.dedupField === 'id' ? 'apollo_id' : config.dedupField]) ?? ''))
           .filter(Boolean)
           .includes(String(r[config.dedupField === 'id' ? 'apollo_id' : config.dedupField] ?? '')))
    .length > 0
shared.table.yaml:
# Everything the three nodes share: the auth, and the url for one table.
#
# The table part may be a NAME ("Companies") or an id ("tbl..."), so it is percent-encoded.
# The base id never needs encoding.

credential: &credential
  scheme: bearer
  token: "{{ credentials.airtableCredential.personalAccessToken }}"

url: &url >-
  return 'https://api.airtable.com/v0/' + config.baseId
    + '/' + encodeURIComponent(config.tableId)

files.api/events.yaml:
# One row per output connector, in interface.yaml order.
#
# A chunked call's reply is { sent, batches, results, errors }, so `inserted` is the two
# chunked calls' `sent` added together and `errors` is both lists concatenated. A skipped
# call leaves no key, which is why each is guarded.

- emit: inserted
  from: response
  value: >-
    return ((calls.updates || {}).sent || 0) + ((calls.creates || {}).sent || 0)

- emit: skipped
  from: response
  value: { $ref: rows#skipped }

- emit: total
  from: response
  value: "return (config.records || []).length"

- emit: errors
  from: response
  value: >-
    return [].concat(((calls.updates || {}).errors || []), ((calls.creates || {}).errors || []))
files.api/run.yaml:
# Four calls, each conditional, and the vendor's limits are what make it four rather than
# one: Airtable takes 10 records per write, so `chunk` repeats the request per slice.
#
# `id` is RESERVED by Airtable, so an upstream row carrying its own `id` that is not an
# Airtable record id has it renamed to `apollo_id` rather than dropped. That mapping came
# from the retired code and is kept verbatim: changing it would silently lose a column.

# Existing values for the dedup field, paged over the whole table. Only the one field is
# requested, so this stays cheap even on a large table.
- name: existing
  when: "return !!String(config.dedupField || '').trim()"
  method: GET
  url: { $ref: table#url }
  credential: { $ref: table#credential }
  query:
    fields: "return config.dedupField === 'id' ? 'apollo_id' : config.dedupField"
  transport: json
  paginate:
    strategy: cursor
    cursor: "return response.offset"
    into: offset
    items: "return response.records"

# Rows that already carry a valid Airtable record id are UPDATES.
- name: updates
  when: "return (config.records || []).filter(r => typeof r.id === 'string' && r.id.length === 17 && r.id.slice(0, 3) === 'rec').length > 0"

  method: PATCH
  url: { $ref: table#url }
  credential: { $ref: table#credential }
  chunk:
    size: 10
    items: { $ref: rows#isAirtableId }
  body: >-
    return { records: batch.map(r => ({
      id: r.id,
      fields: Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(r).filter(e => e[0] !== 'id'))
    })) }
  transport: json

# Everything else is a CREATE, minus anything the dedup field says is already there.
- name: creates
  when: { $ref: rows#toCreateAny }
  method: POST
  url: { $ref: table#url }
  credential: { $ref: table#credential }
  chunk:
    size: 10
    items: { $ref: rows#toCreate }
  body: "return { records: batch.map(r => ({ fields: r })) }"
  transport: json
files.config.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/config.schema.json

configSchema:
  type: object
  required: [baseId, tableId, records]
  properties:
    baseId:
      type: string
      title: Base ID
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    tableId:
      type: string
      title: Table Name or ID
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    records:
      type: array
      title: Records
      description: >-
        The rows to write. An expression, usually reading an upstream node's output. A row
        carrying a valid Airtable id is UPDATED rather than created.
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    dedupField:
      type: string
      title: Dedup Field (optional)
      description: >-
        Skip a new row when this field's value already exists in the table. Existing values
        are read first, paging the whole table.
      default: ""

    # WHO MAY RUN THIS BOX, set by whoever builds the workflow (15-who-can-run-it.md).
    #
    # INSTANCE config, not the manifest's `auth`, and the two answer different questions.
    # The manifest is the node author's FLOOR: "this node is inherently privileged". These
    # are the builder's, per box on the canvas, because the same node type legitimately
    # faces staff on one workflow and customers on another.
    #
    # A role especially has to live here: `finance:approve` is a claim THIS deployment's
    # identity provider mints, and a node published to the marketplace cannot know the role
    # vocabulary of every universe that installs it.
    #
    # The executor takes the STRICTER of the two. Neither can loosen the other.
    authRequired:
      type: boolean
      title: Require sign-in
      description: Only signed-in callers can run this step.
      default: false
      "ui:widget": toggle
    authRole:
      type: string
      title: Require role
      description: A claim the caller must carry, like finance:approve.
      default: ""
      "ui:dependencies": { authRequired: true }

"ui:order": [authRequired, authRole, baseId, tableId, records, dedupField]
files.interface.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/interface.schema.json

inputs:
  - name: input
    type: object
    description: Trigger. The records usually template from an upstream node's output.

outputs:
  - name: inserted
    type: number
    description: Records accepted, across creates and updates
  - name: skipped
    type: number
    description: Records dropped because the dedup field's value was already present
  - name: total
    type: number
    description: Records offered
  - name: errors
    type: array
    description: One entry per failed batch. Empty means every batch landed.

credentials:
  - name: airtableCredential
    required: true
    displayName: Airtable
files.node.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/node.schema.json

type: AirtableInsert
kind: PromiseNode
name: Airtable Insert
category: Storage & Data
color: "#FCB400"
description: Write records to an Airtable table, batched, updating any that carry a record id
whenToUse: >
  Pick to WRITE rows into an Airtable table from upstream data: it batches automatically,
  updates any record that already carries an Airtable id, and can skip rows whose value is
  already present. Use it to persist a collection; it writes, it does not read.

# WHO MAY RUN THIS (DECLARATIVE_NODES.md §9.13). Compulsory on every node, so that a node
# nobody thought about cannot look the same as one deliberately left open.
#
# `required: false` adds no requirement of its own: the node runs for whoever the trigger
# admitted. The trigger instance's publicEntry toggle still owns the door, and requirements
# only ever narrow.
auth:
  required: false

capabilities:
  # NEVER cacheable: reuse would skip the write entirely.
  cacheable: false
files.test.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/test.schema.json

# WRITES. Point this at a scratch table you do not mind adding a row to, then run it. The
# fixture is deliberately one row so a mistake costs one row.
testData:
  config:
    baseId: appXXXXXXXXXXXXXX
    tableId: Scratch
    records:
      - Name: Unoverse bench row
    dedupField: Name
  inputs:
    input: {}
  expect:
    # Either it wrote the row, or dedup found it from a previous run. Both are correct.
    inserted: "return output.inserted + output.skipped === 1"
    errors: "return output.errors.length === 0"
